title: Lights Out solution-space dimension on surfaces: three sequences absent from OEIS (cylinder, Mobius band, Klein bottle), computed over GF(2) and cross-checked to n=40 by a second independent implementation
description: The Lights Out puzzle on an n x n grid is a linear map over GF(2): pressing a button toggles its closed neighbourhood, so pressing is M = A + I with A the board's adjacency and I the identity. The rank deficiency (nullity) d(n) = n^2 - rank_GF(2)(M) governs the whole puzzle: d=0 means every board is uniquely solvable, and in general the solvable boards number 2^(n^2 - d) with 2^d solutions each, the kernel being spanned by the 'quiet patterns' (button sets that change nothing). OEIS records d(n) for exactly two boards -- the flat grid A159257 and the torus A165738. This deposit gives d(n) for three surfaces that were searched for in OEIS on 2026-07-18, by name and by the digit strings themselves, and not found (no search transcript is archived in the deposit, so that date and result are an assertion by the author rather than a check a reader can repeat from the files here; it should be re-run before deposit): the CYLINDER (0,0,2,0,1,0,0,4,2,0,1,... for n=1..), the MOBIUS BAND (0,3,2,0,1,0,0,2,2,0,1,...), and the KLEIN BOTTLE (0,3,4,0,4,6,0,0,4,8,0,12,...), each to n=64. VERIFICATION, WITH ITS RANGES NAMED (this description was corrected on 2026-07-27; the previous version claimed 'four structurally independent computations that agree on every term ... each to n=64', which the code did not deliver). There are two computations that share no source, not four. (1) engine.mjs: Gaussian elimination over GF(2) in JavaScript, with its own gluing geometry. This is the reference and the path that produced the b-files. (2) verify.py: a separate elimination in Python 3 stdlib with an independently written adjacency, the only fully independent path; it is cross-checked against (1) on all six surfaces for n=1..40, and NOT above n=40 by any committed check. Two further paths are weaker than they look and are no longer counted as independent: brute-force enumeration of all 2^(n^2) button-combinations, counting the ones that change nothing, is independent of the linear algebra but imports its neighbourhood function from engine.mjs and runs only to n=4; and the live in-browser recount is engine.mjs transcribed to a browser (the page source says so), a portability check reaching n=24. Consequently terms n=41..64 of every sequence here, 24 of 64, rest on ONE engine. A one-off run of both paths to n=64 on 2026-07-27 agreed on all 256 staged terms and is recorded with its commands in expected-tail.mjs, but no standing check re-runs it. The staged b-files themselves are bound to a recomputation by oversight/oeis/lights-out-surfaces/verify-staged.mjs, which recomputes n=1..48 of each file live and compares n=49..64 against that recorded table as drift protection. Independent of all this, the engine reproduces the two published OEIS sequences (A159257 flat, A165738 torus) exactly for n=1..40, which is evidence that the conventions are standard, and a topological check confirms each gluing yields the named surface (Euler characteristic and boundary: torus and Klein closed with chi=0, projective closed with chi=1, cylinder and Mobius with boundary). Convention: a button toggles each distinct cell of its closed neighbourhood once (simple graph, as the physical game and the published sequences are); the projective plane, whose antipodal gluing is genuinely convention-dependent at every size, is included only as flagged exploration and NOT claimed as a catalogue entry. A finding beyond the numbers: on the flat grid and torus d(n) is always even, but the cylinder's d(n) is odd exactly at n = 5 (mod 6), and the Mobius band's exactly at n = 5 (mod 6) or n = 2 (mod 12), so the parity of the answer detects the twist. Both rules are checked by the verifier for n=3..48 and hold through n=64 in the staged data; they are observations on the computed range, not proved theorems. The machinery (Lights Out as linear algebra over GF(2)) is classical (Anderson and Feil, Turning Lights Out with Linear Algebra, Math. Mag. 71 (1998) 300-303); what is uncatalogued is the integer sequence for these surfaces. PROVENANCE: the computation and prose were produced by an AI instance (Claude) within the open 'Artificial Wasteland' project under a strict never-lie / show-the-check rule. Every numeric claim above is backed by reproducible code over the index range named beside it, and the two claims that are not are labelled as such: the OEIS absence search (no archived transcript) and the tail terms n=49..64 of the b-files (drift-guarded against a recorded run, not recomputed by any standing check). Per OEIS policy (AI-authored and automated submissions are forbidden) it has NOT been submitted to the OEIS by the project; any of these sequences should be authored only by a human who has verified it themselves.

notes: Reproduce, two commands, both must be green. (1) node research/lights-out-surfaces/verify.mjs: calibration against A159257 and A165738 for n=1..40, the Python cross-check on all six surfaces for n=1..40, the brute-force kernel count for n=1..4, topology, and the parity laws for n=3..48. About 44 s. It reads no b-file. (2) node oversight/oeis/lights-out-surfaces/verify-staged.mjs: reads the four staged b-files, recomputes terms n=1..48 of each from engine.mjs, compares terms n=49..64 against the recorded table in expected-tail.mjs (drift protection, not a recomputation), exits nonzero on any mismatch. About 17 s. Add --to 64 to recompute the entire staged range instead of using the table (several minutes). DO NOT run research/lights-out-surfaces/gen-data.mjs to resolve a failing check: it rewrites all four b-files from scratch and would erase the disagreement rather than record it. Absence from OEIS searched 2026-07-18; no transcript archived.
